headline: High-risk shared filesystem and unsandboxed server-side code make Langflow→PaddleOCR pair vulnerable to leakage, conflicts, and cascading errors by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can write/read the server filesystem and chain multiple agents; PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can run browsers. If Langflow passes uploaded or generated file content into PaddleOCR, attacker-controlled text in documents could influence downstream parsing. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Langflow forwards untrusted document text into PaddleOCR without provenance tagging
IF PaddleOCR output is later interpreted as instructions by a downstream flow node
mitigations: Add a strict content-type gate before OCR input
Prefix all OCR outputs as untrusted data in flow prompts
Disable any instruction-following step on OCR text
requires-engineering: add provenance labels between flow nodes

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow touches flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and server filesystem files; PaddleOCR touches documents and images. A shared workspace or uploaded-file path would let both agents see the same sensitive documents, and Langflow’s broad network egress increases the chance those contents leave the environment through configured model/API calls. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or upload directory
IF Langflow sends file contents to configured model providers or HTTP services
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Restrict Langflow flows from reading raw sensitive files
Use redacted copies for OCR
Review outbound endpoints in Langflow flows
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow can write the server filesystem and spawn subprocesses; PaddleOCR can run browsers and call APIs. If both operate on shared mutable resources, they can overwrite each other’s files or race on intermediate artifacts. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so the conflict pathway exists in default deployments with shared storage.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or artifact store
IF the orchestrator does not provide file-level locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Make intermediate artifacts read-only after creation
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Avoid shared temp paths
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is a graph-based orchestrator that can chain multiple agents, while PaddleOCR produces extracted text from documents/images. That makes it plausible for Langflow to treat OCR output as authoritative input to later steps without verification. The pair therefore has a default cascade path from extraction errors into downstream actions, though not necessarily irreversible.
conditions: IF Langflow routes PaddleOCR output directly into a decision or action node
IF no validation step checks OCR confidence or schema before use
mitigations: Insert a human review step for low-confidence OCR
Validate OCR output against expected schema
Keep OCR output separate from action prompts
Log and sample-check extracted fields
requires-engineering: add confidence-based gating

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow stores per-flow credentials and processes flow inputs/intermediate outputs, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different handling of sensitive document data versus orchestration state. That creates a compliance gap only if regulated documents are routed through both without aligned retention and access controls.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by both agents
IF retention or access-control policies differ between Langflow stores and PaddleOCR outputs
mitigations: Document retention rules for both systems
Minimize stored OCR artifacts
Restrict access to Langflow secrets store
Delete temporary document copies promptly
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
